14       FINANCIAL QUALIFICATIONS

This chapter of the safety evaluation (SE) describes the U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission
(NRC or Commission) staff’s review and evaluation of Long Mott Energy, LLC’s (LME) financial
qualifications as presented in Part I, “General and Financial Information,” of revision 1 of the
Long Mott Generating Station (LMGS) construction permit (CP) application (Agencywide
Documents and Access Management System (ADAMS) Accession No. ML26261A423), as well
as LME’s requested exemption from the financial qualification requirements in Title 10 of the
Code of Federal Regulations (10 CFR) 50.33(f) and 10 CFR Part 50, “Domestic Licensing of
Production and Utilization Facilities,” Appendix C, “A Guide for the Financial Data and Related
Information Required to Establish Financial Qualifications for Construction Permits and
Combined Licenses” in Part V, “Non-Applicabilities and Exemptions,” of the CP application
(ML26261A427). In a letter dated March 3, 2026, LME submitted a proprietary supplement to
Part I of the CP application (ML26062A842), which was included in revision 1 of the CP
application (ML26261A419). With certain exceptions, a Part 50 application is required to provide
sufficient information to demonstrate to the Commission, the financial qualification of the
applicant to carry out, in accordance with regulations in 10 CFR Part 50, the activities for which
the permit or license is sought. The applicable regulatory requirements for the evaluation of the
LME’s financial qualifications are as follows:

     •   10 CFR 50.33, “Contents of applications; general information,”

     •   10 CFR Part 50, Appendix C,

     •   10 CFR 50.38, “Ineligibility of certain applicants,”

     •   10 CFR 50.54, “Conditions of licenses,”

     •   10 CFR 70.23, “Requirements for approval of applications,” and

     •   10 CFR Part 140, “Financial Protection Requirements and Indemnity Agreements.”

     •   The applicable guidance for the evaluation of LME’s financial qualifications is: DANU-
         ISG-2022-01, section 16, “Financial Qualification and Insurance and Liability.”

In addition, the NRC staff considered the Financial Qualifications for Reactor Licensing
Rulemaking dated November 16, 2016 (ML15322A185). The NRC staff evaluated the financial
qualifications in section 14.1 and the exemption request in section 14.2, of this SE chapter1.

14.1     Financial Ability to Construct LMGS

14.1.1 Construction Costs

1 By memorandum dated June 25, 2026, the NRC’s Atomic and Safety Licensing Board denied San Antonio Bay

Estuarine Waterkeeper’s (intervenor) contentions associated with this review area (ML26176A482).
                           OFFICIAL USE ONLY – PROPRIETARY INFORMATION
                          OFFICIAL USE ONLY – PROPRIETARY INFORMATION



Technical Evaluation

The NRC staff reviewed the projected costs for the construction of the proposed LMGS facility
provided in CP application part I, table I-1, “Estimates of Long Mott Generating Station
Construction Costs (2024 dollars).” The total estimated projected costs include estimates for
total nuclear production plant costs, transmission, distribution, general plant costs, and nuclear
fuel inventory cost for the first core for each of the four reactor modules comprising the LMGS
design.

The NRC staff evaluated the sufficiency of the information provided for the LMGS construction
and related fuel cycle costs. The NRC staff evaluated the sufficiency of this information against
the financial qualification standard under 10 CFR Part 70, “Domestic Licensing of Special
Nuclear Material,” based on the exemption request that is evaluated in SE section 14.2.

The NRC staff’s review of the application identified that LME’s construction cost estimate
included a detailed breakdown of the cost elements including the factors related to facility
preparation and development, equipment and supplies, and labor (corporate and construction)
factors. Additionally, the cost estimate was developed with support from the Dow Chemical
Company (TDCC), which is LME’s parent company. Based on the NRC staff’s review of LME’s
construction cost estimate in section 2.1 of Part I of the CP application, the NRC staff
determined that LME used an appropriate approach to assess the size and scope of
construction. Additionally, the NRC staff reviewed LME’s relationship with TDCC. Further, based
on the information provided in Part I of the CP application, which includes examples of active
and completed “large-build megaprojects” managed by TDCC, the NRC staff determined that
TDCC has significant experience in capital sourcing, designing, procuring, and implementing
“large-build megaprojects” globally. This gives the NRC staff additional confidence that the
projected construction cost values are reasonable.

Based on the NRC staff’s evaluation of the cost estimates for LMGS and its relationship with
TDCC, the NRC staff determined that LME’s cost estimate is reasonable.

14.1.2 Financial Qualifications

Consistent with the NRC staff’s determination on the requested exemption as discussed in SE
section 14.2, the NRC staff evaluated LME’s financial qualifications using the standard
described in 10 CFR 70.23(a)(5). Under this requirement, the NRC staff must determine
whether the applicant “appears to be” financially qualified to engage in the proposed activities.

Technical Evaluation

The NRC staff reviewed part I of the LME CP application and evaluated whether LME meets the
financial qualification requirement in 10 CFR 70.23(a)(5). As discussed in section 14.2 of this
SE, the NRC staff determined that an exemption from the CP financial qualification
requirements in 10 CFR 50.33(f) and 10 CFR Part 50, Appendix C, is warranted, as requested
in Part V – Non-Applicabilities and Exemptions of the CP application.

Appendix A to part I of the CP application contains a financial capacity plan (FCP) which
includes a construction cost estimate. The FCP demonstrates LME’s understanding of the size
and scope of construction of LMGS, including the level of capital necessary to undertake the

                         OFFICIAL USE ONLY – PROPRIETARY INFORMATION
                             OFFICIAL USE ONLY – PROPRIETARY INFORMATION


project. The FCP also discusses the organizational and human resources, experience, skills,
and expertise required to obtain proper financing and ultimately finance the project.

The NRC staff evaluated LME’s demonstration of reasonable assurance that it will obtain
funding for construction that is equal to or more than 50 percent of the LMGS construction cost
estimate. To determine if the applicant “appears to be” financially qualified, the NRC staff
considered section 7.2.1.2 of the regulatory basis for the Financial Qualifications for Reactor
Licensing Rulemaking. In reviewing an applicant’s financial qualifications, the NRC staff
recognizes the committed sources of funding described in an application as contributing to
financial qualification requirements and considers applicants that have greater than 50 percent
committed funding sources at the time of the application, to appear to be financially qualified.

The NRC staff evaluated the “Financial Support Agreement Between Dow Chemical Company
and Long Mott Energy, LLC” (FSA) dated February 23, 2026, that established that LME’s parent
company, TDCC, will provide financial support to LME for construction of the LMGS
(ML26062A842). The financial support agreement was incorporated in the revision 1 of the CP
application and includes the parent company’s agreement to provide funding for construction
costs up to a specified dollar amount unless the parent company procures a substitute loan
facility and/or a letter of credit that meets the NRC’s financial assurance requirements and
obtains the NRC’s written consent for such substitution. The amount of committed funding is
more than 50 percent of the projected construction cost estimate for the LMGS. This financial
support agreement provides a mechanism for LME to incur project costs prior to receiving
federal reimbursement through the U.S. Department of Energy’s (DOE) Advanced Reactor
Demonstration Program (ARDP). Based on the committed funding provided through the FSA
between TDCC and LME, the NRC staff has determined that LME demonstrates that it appears
to be financially qualified by establishing that it has secured greater than 50 percent of the
required construction funding for the LMGS.

Accordingly, based on its review of the FCP and the FSA, the NRC staff determined that the
level of detail provided by LME related to its understanding of the size and scope of constructing
the LMGS, its parent company’s experience in other large-scale projects such as the examples
provided in part I of the CP application, and the company’s agreement to provide 50 percent or
more of the estimated cost of construction is sufficient to meet 10 CFR 70.23(a)(5)2. Therefore,
based on these considerations including the current level of committed funds, the NRC staff
finds that LME “appears to be financially qualified” to construct the LMGS.

14.1.3 Conclusion

Based on the NRC staff’s conclusions above, the NRC staff finds that the information provided
by LME regarding its financial ability to construct the LMGS is sufficient and that LME meets the
10 CFR Part 70 standard of “appears to be financially qualified” for the proposed activities.

14.2    Request for Exemption Regarding Financial Qualifications

In part V of the CP application (ML26261A427), LME requested an exemption under 10 CFR
50.12(a)(2)(ii) and 10 CFR 50.12(a)(2)(vi) from the financial qualification requirements in 10

2 The NRC’s Atomic Safety and Licensing Board reached a similar conclusion in Long Mott Energy, LLC (Long Mott

Generating Station), LBP-26-4 (June 25, 2026), appeal pending, (dismissing Contention 3B and finding that LME had
demonstrated at least 50 percent of the funding required to construct LMGS).

                            OFFICIAL USE ONLY – PROPRIETARY INFORMATION
                          OFFICIAL USE ONLY – PROPRIETARY INFORMATION


CFR 50.33(f), and 10 CFR Part 50, Appendix C. Per the applicant’s submittal, under this
exemption request, the NRC would apply the financial qualification standard required for 10
CFR Part 70 applicants (for licenses to receive title to, own, acquire, deliver, receive, possess,
use and transfer special nuclear material) as described in 10 CFR 70.23(a)(5), in lieu of the
financial qualification standards in 10 CFR 50.33(f), and 10 CFR Part 50, Appendix C.
Specifically, LME requests that it be permitted to demonstrate that it appears to be financially
qualified for the issuance of a CP rather than being required to meet the requirements of 10
CFR 50.33(f) and 10 CFR Part 50, Appendix C.

Issuance of this exemption would, in effect, allow the use of the 10 CFR Part 70 financial
qualification standard, normally used for licensing the possession and use of special nuclear
material, for the construction of the LMGS.

14.2.1 Technical Evaluation

The requested exemption would exempt LME from the financial qualification requirements in
10 CFR 50.33(f) and 10 CFR Part 50, Appendix C. As stated above, 10 CFR 50.12(a) allows the
NRC to grant exemptions from regulations, should certain criteria be met. This exemption
evaluation focuses on LME’s proposal to use the 10 CFR Part 70 standard of “appears to be
financially qualified.” This section of the SE describes the NRC staff’s evaluation of the
exemption request.

As further discussed below, the NRC staff concludes that LME’s exemption request satisfies the
following provisions in 10 CFR 50.12(a):

The Exemption is Authorized by Law

The Commission has the authority to issue LME’s requested exemption. The exemption would
not conflict with any provision of the Atomic Energy Act (AEA) of 1954, as amended, or any
other law. In particular, the NRC has broad discretion to prescribe requirements for financial
qualifications, as provided in section 182(a) of the AEA. As such, the requested exemption is
authorized by law.

The Exemption Presents no Undue Risk to Public Health and Safety

The NRC staff evaluated LME’s request for an exemption from the requirements of
10 CFR 50.33(f) and 10 CFR Part 50, Appendix C, to determine if it presents an undue risk to
public health and safety. To support the NRC staff’s evaluation, the NRC staff reviewed
information provided by the applicant in part V of the CPA, which states that the exemption does
not pertain to any NRC safety requirements that directly govern design or construction activities
for the LMGS and the use of the 10 CFR 70 financial qualification standards for LMGS
construction would not compromise public health and safety. Additionally, the applicant
referenced the NRC’s regulatory basis document for the proposed amendment to the financial
requirement in 10 CFR Part 50 (ML15322A185), which explains how the agency’s oversight
programs ensure public health and safety and states that an applicant demonstrating
commitments for at least 50 percent of construction funding provides a sufficient demonstration
of financial capacity.

In an NRC staff requirements memorandum (SRM) titled “Policy Options for Merchant (Non-
Electric Utility) Plant Financial Qualifications” (SRM-SECY-13-0124), the Commission approved

                         OFFICIAL USE ONLY – PROPRIETARY INFORMATION
                         OFFICIAL USE ONLY – PROPRIETARY INFORMATION


the NRC staff’s recommendation to conduct a rulemaking and directed the NRC staff to amend
the financial qualification requirements in 10 CFR Part 50, to conform to the financial
qualification review standard in 10 CFR Part 70 (ML14114A358). In response to the SRM, the
NRC staff developed a proposed rule; in the regulatory basis for the proposed Financial
Qualifications for Reactor Licensing Rulemaking (ML15322A185), the NRC staff stated that:

       The NRC staff believes that an applicant with commitments for at least 50
       percent of its construction funding has made a sufficient demonstration of
       financial capacity. … Accordingly, where the applicant has identified such
       commitments, a license condition requiring documentation for the remaining
       portion of the construction funding is not necessary. This is because the purpose
       of the NRC staff’s review is not to ensure that the project is completed; rather, it
       is to ensure that an applicant has the financial capacity to obtain financing when
       the project moves forward.

In addition, SECY-13-0124, “Policy Options for Merchant (Non-Electric Utility) Plant Financial
Qualifications,” (ML13057A006) states the following:

       Commission history and precedent has consistently shown an ongoing concern
       for the potential of degraded safety in the face of degraded financial
       qualifications. However, this history also consistently indicates a Commission
       belief that any nexus between safety and the NRC’s review of financial
       qualifications is indirect and of secondary importance to ensuring public health
       and safety. Furthermore, it is clear that Section 182a. of the AEA grants the
       Commission much flexibility in the area of financial qualifications requirements.

Additionally, as discussed in SECY-79-299, “Generic Issue of Financial Qualifications
(ML12236A723), the Commission previously concluded that financial qualification reviews are
only one part of the NRC’s safety oversight of nuclear power reactor applications. As the
Commission observed,

       although technical reviews and inspection efforts are very effective direct
       methods of discovering deficiencies that could affect safety, the analysis of
       financial qualifications is an additional method, albeit indirect, of determining an
       applicant’s ability to satisfy safety requirements. The financial qualifications
       review is one element in the Commission’s system of multiple and redundant
       safety reviews and inspections. The purpose of the financial qualifications review
       in this system is analogous to the overlapping protective echelons of the
       ‘defense-in-depth’ approach used in designing nuclear power plants.

These regulatory program assessments underscore the indirect effect resulting from the
financial qualifications review, as compared to more direct safety evaluations, in assuring the
safety of a proposed facility. Further, the NRC staff notes that the direct means to ensure safety
include a detailed technical licensing review of CP applications, the construction reactor
oversight process, the vendor inspection program, and the quality assurance inspection
program.

Further, various programs described in the CP application, support a determination as to
whether the LMGS will be safely constructed. These programs include the LMGS quality
assurance program and the reliability and integrity management program which are described in

                        OFFICIAL USE ONLY – PROPRIETARY INFORMATION
                         OFFICIAL USE ONLY – PROPRIETARY INFORMATION


section 8.1 and section 8.2 of the Preliminary Safety Analysis Report, respectively and are
evaluated in sections 8.1 and 8.2 of this SE. Additionally, the applicant used the licensing
modernization project (LMP) methodology, which provided a structured approach to
development of the licensing basis that enables a comprehensive understanding of the risk and
safety-significance of the facility’s structures, systems, and components (SSCs). This
understanding enables both the applicant and the NRC staff to properly evaluate the risk and
safety-significance of SSCs during construction, ensuring that resources are strategically
allocated to maintain facility safety and support informed regulatory oversight of construction-
related changes.

Although the applicant is requesting an exemption from the financial requirements of
10 CFR 50.33(f) and 10 CFR Part 50, Appendix C, the requested exemption proposes to apply
the 10 CFR Part 70 financial qualification requirements. The NRC staff’s evaluation of the
applicant’s financial qualifications against the 10 CFR Part 70 requirements is provided in
section 14.1 of this SE, in which the NRC staff concluded that LME had adequately
demonstrated that it meets the 10 CFR Part 70 requirement. While the financial qualification
criterion in 10 CFR Part 70 is different than the requirement in 10 CFR Part 50, the NRC staff
has determined that the applicant meets the financial qualifications requirement in 10 CFR
Part 70 and, that this demonstration, in combination with the applicant’s use of the LMP
approach, establishes that the applicant appears to be financially qualified to conduct the
activities proposed in the CP application.

Given the NRC staff’s established reactor oversight programs, the applicant’s programs
supporting the safe construction and operation of the facility, the proposed funding for
construction of the LMGS provided in the financial support agreement, and the applicant’s
proposal to apply the 10 CFR Part 70 alternative financial qualification requirements for the CP
application, the NRC staff has concluded that the issuance of the exemption would not have an
adverse effect on public health and safety.

The Exemption is Consistent with the Common Defense and Security

The requested exemption pertains only to the financial qualification requirements for LMGS and
does not affect any security requirements for LMGS. Therefore, the NRC staff has determined
that the exemption request is consistent with the common defense and security.

Special Circumstances

The NRC staff evaluated whether special circumstances are present, as required in
10 CFR 50.12(a)(2). In its exemption request, LME asserts that the special circumstances
required in 10 CFR 50.12(a)(2)(ii) are present, specifically that application of the financial
qualification requirements in 10 CFR 50.33(f) and Appendix C, are not necessary to achieve the
underlying purpose of the rule. As discussed above, the purpose of the financial qualification
regulations for CPs in 10 CFR 50.33(f) and 10 CFR Part 50, Appendix C, is to prevent safety
issues from occurring that might result from underfunding during construction.

In its exemption request and supplements, LME states that it is participating in the DOE’s ARDP
and that this meets the showing of special circumstances required in 10 CFR 50.12(a)(2)(vi).
The NRC staff evaluated whether participation in DOE’s ARDP is a special circumstance under
10 CFR 50.12(a)(2)(vi). As described in “Funding Opportunity Announcement-Advanced
Reactor Demonstration Program,” dated May 14, 2020, the ARDP is structured as a public-

                        OFFICIAL USE ONLY – PROPRIETARY INFORMATION
                         OFFICIAL USE ONLY – PROPRIETARY INFORMATION


private partnership in which the DOE and industry jointly share the financial burden associated
with the development and deployment of advanced nuclear reactors. Further, the NRC staff
determined that the ARDP supports Executive Order 14300, “Ordering the Reform of the
Nuclear Regulatory Commission,” because section 2, “Policy,” states, in part, that it is the policy
of the United States to:

   (a) Reestablish the United States as the global leader in nuclear energy;

   (b) Facilitate increased deployment of new nuclear reactor technologies, such as
       Generation III+ and IV reactors, modular reactors, and microreactors, including by
       lowering regulatory and cost barriers to entry;

   (c) Facilitate the expansion of American nuclear energy capacity from approximately
       100 GW [gigawatt] in 2024 to 400 GW by 2050;

   (d) Employ emerging technologies to safely accelerate the modeling, simulation, testing,
       and approval of new reactor designs.

ARDP funding is disbursed on a reimbursement basis, in incremental intervals, contingent upon
the applicant’s expenditure of funds. As the ARDP operates on a reimbursement model, the
applicant must possess sufficient upfront capital to incur project costs prior to receiving ADRP
reimbursement. Based on the ARDP funding and the applicant’s financial qualifications
evaluated by the NRC staff in section 14.2 of this SE, the NRC staff finds that safety lapses
would not occur as a result of underfunding during the construction of the facility. Thus, the
application of the financial qualification requirements in 10 CFR 50.33(f) and 10 CFR Part 50,
Appendix C, is not necessary to achieve the underlying purpose of the regulation in this case,
and special circumstances are present, in accordance with 10 CFR 50.12(a)(2)(ii).

The ARDP and the Executive Order are material circumstances that did not exist at the time the
regulatory requirement for which the exemption is being sought, was issued. Because the
ARDP aligns with the goals of the Executive Order, which establishes a national interest in the
development of nuclear power alternatives such as the LMGS, the NRC staff finds that the
objectives of the ARDP are clearly in the public interest. Furthermore, the NRC staff determined
that the selection of LMGS by DOE as part of its ARDP funding, supports the United States
policy as described above, and therefore, the NRC staff determined that LME’s requested
exemption is in the public interest, in accordance with 10 CFR 50.12(a)(2)(vi).

Based on the above, the NRC staff finds that the application of the financial qualification
requirements in 10 CFR 50.33(f) and 10 CFR Part 50, Appendix C, is not necessary to achieve
the underlying purpose of the regulation in this case, and that special circumstances in
accordance with 10 CFR 50.12(a)(2)(ii) and 10 CFR 50.12(a)(2)(vi), are present.

14.2.2 Conclusion

The NRC staff finds that an exemption from the financial qualifications requirements under
10 CFR 50.33(f), and 10 CFR Part 50, Appendix C, is acceptable because it is authorized by
law, will not present undue risk to public health and safety, is consistent with common defense
and security, and special circumstances are present.

14.3   Foreign Ownership, Control, or Domination

Section 50.38 of 10 CFR, “Ineligibility of Certain Applicants,” states: “Any person who is a
citizen, national, or agent of a foreign country, or any corporation, or other entity which the
Commission knows or has reason to believe is owned, controlled, or dominated by an alien, a
foreign corporation, or a foreign government, shall be ineligible to apply for and obtain a
license.” Section 2.4, “Foreign Ownership, or Control,” of part 1 to the LMGS CP application
describes the ownership and control of LME. This section of the CP application states that
foreign entities do not possess the ability to vote or control decisions and cannot dominate LME.

14.3.1 Technical Evaluation

The NRC staff evaluated LME following the guidance provided in the “Final Standard Review
Plan on Foreign Ownership, Control, or Domination” published in the Federal Register on
September 28, 1999 (64 FR 52355), to determine whether an applicant is owned, controlled, or
dominated by an alien, a foreign corporation, or a foreign government.

The LMGS CP application states that: “LME is a U.S. company. […] LME is managed and
controlled by TDCC [The Dow Chemical Company] via TDCC’s wholly owned subsidiary GWNH
[GWN Holding, LLC], an intermediate holding company that operates as a direct, wholly owned
subsidiary of TDCC, both of which are also U.S. companies. In turn, TDCC is a wholly owned
subsidiary of Dow Inc., a U.S. company that is publicly traded (NYSE: DOW) with no material
foreign ownership of publicly traded shares.” Additionally, LME provided the names, addresses,
and citizenships of the TDCC and Dow, Inc. directors and principal officers, which are described
in table I-3, and the names, addresses, and citizenships of the principal officers of GWNH,
which are provided in table I-4.

The NRC staff conducted an independent analysis, including open-source research and
verification of the information provided in the CP application, and found no evidence of foreign
ownership, control, or domination (FOCD). Based on its review, the NRC staff does not know or
have reason to believe that LME is owned, controlled, or dominated by a foreign interest.

14.3.2 Conclusion

In summary, based on the NRC staff’s evaluation, the NRC staff concludes that the information
provided by the applicant on FOCD is sufficient and that the application meets the requirements
in 10 CFR 50.38.

14.4   Nuclear Insurance and Indemnity

LME did not provide nuclear insurance and indemnity information in its CP application. LME will
be required to obtain insurance in accordance with 10 CFR 50.54(w), and to satisfy the financial
protection and indemnity requirements in 10 CFR 140.11, “Amounts of financial protection for
certain reactors,” prior to loading fuel. The NRC staff will review the sufficiency of LME’s
insurance and financial protection and indemnity provisions during its review of LME’s expected
operating license application.
